title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre - Stanford University on 1982-10-10
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/88.2k) -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC/24 (1 DVD FLAC)
source: (FOB) Sony ECM-220T -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Fuji Metal Tape/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: An outstanding audience recording of the Oct 10‑1982 Frost show – crisp, warm and PHAT sound paired with a high‑energy performance highlighted by Crazy Fingers→Lost Sailor→Saint and a soaring Throwing Stones jam.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this tape’s pure, full‑bodied audio captured with modest Sony ECM‑220T mics, noting only occasional background chatter and a slightly thin low end. The concert itself is described as electric, with standout moments like Crazy Fingers → Lost Sailor → Saint of Circumstance, a superb Throwing Stones jam, Baby Blue and Morning Dew, while the Touch is deemed flat and Jerry’s vocals are criticized on one occasion.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (10‑plus) give 5‑star praise for both the performance and recording; only a few mixed or low‑star comments are present, yielding an overall rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Recorded with Sony ECM‑220T mics placed above the audience; reviewers call it crisp, warm, full and PHAT. Minor issues: slight background conversation and a less deep bottom end, but overall superb for an audience tape.

standout_songs: Crazy Fingers > Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance
poor_songs: Crazy Fingers (as noted by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Conventional setlist but packed with electricity; first set praised for its strength, second set highlighted by seamless transitions and powerful jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Strong guitar work noted on several tracks (e.g., Playin', Baby Blue) but one reviewer criticizes his vocal tone as weak and lacking confidence that night.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is credited with saving the show, delivering strong vocals on Baby Blue and Morning Dew; overall praised for his energy.
